then.text: The lambs are back, all three, and all of them smug about it. Thank you.
Loaghtan sheep sometimes have four horns. Mostly they have attitude.

else.text: Ah. A visitor. Don't suppose you've seen three Loaghtan lambs? Brown, small, certain they own the island.
They got out of the field this morning. They know how to open the gate. I've never taught them. I don't want to know.
If you find them, give them a word. They'll follow you back. They like new people. They don't like me.

then.text: All three! Bless you. Here, take this. A Silver Snare. My uncle used it on a sea monster. Allegedly. It was a seal.

else.text: Two back and one to go. The last one is the cleverest. Look somewhere with a good view of me.
Some of them are back, but not all. Keep looking along the fences.
Still missing, the little scamps. They'll be in the field somewhere, hiding in plain sight.

sailor.text: Back to Liverpool? The boat goes when the tide agrees.

rail_guard.text: Douglas Station. Steam trains to Port Erin, horse trams along the prom.
Trains to the mainland? Love, it's an island. You'll want the ferry for that.

tram_driver.text: Horse trams have run along this prom since 1876. The oldest surviving horse tramway in the world.
Our horses get the winter off. Lucky horses.

tt_fan.text: The Isle of Man TT races started in 1907. Bikes at over 120 miles an hour, past people's front gardens.
My nan's front hedge has been clipped by seven world champions.

cat_lady.text: That's a Manx cat. No tail. Well, almost none. The ones with none at all are rumpies. The ones with a tiny stump are stumpies.
A Manx cat can't wag a tail at you. You'll have to guess whether it likes you.

kipper_man.text: Manx kippers are smoked over oak chippings. The island's been doing it for well over a hundred years.
If you smell this on your coat for days, you've been shopping well.

tynwald_guide.text: Tynwald is the Manx parliament. It's more than a thousand years old. Arguably the oldest in the world to be running continuously.
Every July they sit on a hill and read the laws out loud, in Manx and English. Takes ages. Free tea after.

lamb_1.text: Baa. (It looks at you as if you were the lost one.)
The Loaghtan lamb trots off towards the farmer's gate.

lamb_2.text: Baa. (It looks at you as if you were the lost one.)
The Loaghtan lamb trots off towards the farmer's gate.

lamb_3.text: Baa. (It looks at you as if you were the lost one.)
The Loaghtan lamb trots off towards the farmer's gate.

then.text: The little folk say you're always welcome. I'd say the same, but I can't match their tone.
Mind you say good morning on the way out, though. It's only polite.

else.text: This is the Fairy Bridge, near enough. Every Manx driver says hello to the little folk when they cross. Every single one. Even the grumpy ones.
You greet them or you risk a flat tyre, a lost sock or a very odd Tuesday. I've never found out which. I'm not risking it.
The little folk, the Mooinjer Veggey, are listening. Say hello?

then.text: Hello, little folk. Thank you for having us. I hope the road's been kind.
Nothing. The wind, the gulls, the tram bell in the distance. And then, under the bridge, a tiny voice answers, and it laughs, and it is the nicest sound you have ever heard.
Well, would you look at that. In thirty years they've never once answered me. You must have the knack.
Something light drops into your hand. A ribbon, no longer than a finger, in a green that doesn't quite belong to any tree you know.
They've something else for you, I think. They do like to be thorough. Steady now.
That's them. Say goodbye on the way out. And thank you, love, from every driver on the island.

else.text: Oh, they've gone quiet. They'll be back under the bridge. Say hello again whenever you like.
You walk on. Behind you, something, somewhere, tuts very softly. It's difficult to say whether it's offended or just disappointed.
Oh, you didn't. Well. It's not too late. Have another think and come back.
A little stone bridge over a trickle of a stream. It looks like any bridge. The tram bell rings in the distance.
